summary: Route deprecated Function.caller / Function.arguments observation through runtime compatibility rather than C# stack/delegate reflection.

target.notes: These legacy properties have strict-mode restrictions and implementation-sensitive legacy behavior. They are not equivalent to C# reflection or StackTrace.

caveats: Do not expose C# call stack as JS caller semantics.
Function.prototype has poison-pill accessor behavior for caller/arguments.
references: ECMAScript 2026 Language Specification Restricted Function Properties / legacy caller

tests.name: strict caller restricted
tests.input: function f(){'use strict'; return f.caller;} try{f()}catch(e){console.log(e instanceof TypeError)}
tests.expected_behavior: throws TypeError in the restricted case

tests.name: do not synthesize stack trace
tests.input: function a(){return b()} function b(){return b.caller} console.log(a()===a);
tests.expected_behavior: legacy behavior must be supplied only by compatible runtime
